audience: Mixed software developers in the formative challenge; a later named-role applicant pool and authorized employers in separate studies.
problem: Engineering hiring consumes candidate and team time while often relying on signals that may not transfer to creative, technical and cooperative work.
value_proposition: Offer a short developer challenge with evidence-linked feedback, and test whether no more than three ten-minute case answers can later support a role-specific decision aid.
participants: engineering hiring teams under a separate authorized use
value_mechanism: Versioned cases elicit reasoning, design and coordination choices; human-reviewed evidence-linked rubrics and independent validation test whether these signals transfer to work.
first_order_principles: Three scored sessions maximum and ten recorded minutes per session are a falsifiable product constraint.
Session 1 explicitly targets analysis, creativity and ingenuity through unusual problems.
Participant feedback and employer selection are separate purposes.
An assessment score is not its own independent job outcome.
assumptions: Invited mixed developers will understand and find the formative feedback useful.
Case versions can elicit observable behaviors across relevant backgrounds.
A one-case-per-session design may retain enough precision for some future use.
A role-specific compact policy may reach predeclared selection-quality targets.

intended_outcomes.statement: Developers can complete an accessible three-session challenge within the recorded-time cap.
Developers understand and can act on feedback tied to their answer evidence.
Cases and scoring preserve relevant evidence with measurable uncertainty.
For a named role and capacity, the compact policy meets a fixed absolute target, is non-inferior to a longer pipeline and superior to an equal-time comparator on independent outcomes.
Where independently supported and authorized, the offering saves meaningful effort and sustains a useful product.

boundaries: The first mixed-developer pilot cannot validate employment selection.
No participant collection, employer access or external predictive claim is authorized by this candidate.

hypotheses.statement: Evidence-linked challenge feedback is understood and supports a concrete next practice step for invited mixed developers.
Session 1 adds held-out prediction of useful creative engineering work beyond rivals and other sessions.
Session 2 adds held-out prediction of independent design quality beyond rivals and other sessions.
Session 3 adds held-out prediction of observed coordination beyond rivals and other sessions.

For one predeclared role and capacity, three ten-minute cases reach an absolute utility floor, are non-inferior to a longer pipeline and outperform an equal-time method without unacceptable access or fairness cost.
Where use is validated and authorized, the assessment produces meaningful candidate and employer value after time, operating and access costs.

revision_criteria: Unstable case/rater/mode results for one-case sessions.
Failure of any session to transfer to independent work.
Failure of the three-by-ten comparison or unacceptable access, privacy or fairness cost.
Poor participant feedback usefulness or product value.
